cases.title: fix(streaming): call stream.abort() explicitly when request is aborted (#3042)
cases.bug: abort subscribers are called bare, so a throwing or rejecting listener stops the rest or is unhandled

matched.title: abort() runs subscribers unguarded; one failing listener breaks the rest
matched.failure: A user registers onAbort(() => { throw new Error('x') }) before a cleanup listener. The request is aborted and the first listener throws. The built-in reader.cancel() subscriber, registered first, has already run, but the user's cleanup listener registered afterward is skipped. Because aborted is already true, it is never retried.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading confirmed the case but judged it pre existing, not a defect (abort() still runs subscribers in a bare forEach, so a sync throw skips the later listeners and a rejected async one goes unhandled. The old cancel path did exactly the same, and the new signal-triggered call adds a trigger but no new failure.)
